source: Figure 2b and Tables 3-4 of the paper

studies.author: Aguirre
studies.title: An area within human ventral cortex sensitive to ``building'' stimuli: Evidence and implications
studies.claim: PPA responds more strongly to buildings than to faces or objects.

studies.author: Rajimehr
studies.title: The “parahippocampal place area” responds preferentially to high spatial frequencies in humans and monkeys
studies.claim: PPA responds more strongly to a rectilinear cube than to a matched curvilinear sphere.

studies.author: Bryan
studies.title: Rectilinear edge selectivity is insufficient to explain the category selectivity of the parahippocampal place area
studies.claim: PPA responds more strongly to scenes than to faces even when rectilinearity is matched.

studies.author: Kamps
studies.title: The occipital place area represents the local elements of scenes
studies.claim: PPA responds more strongly to intact rooms than to fractured rooms.

studies.author: Berman
studies.title: Scene content is predominantly conveyed by high spatial frequencies in scene-selective visual cortex
studies.claim: PPA responds more strongly to high-spatial-frequency scenes than to low-spatial-frequency scenes.

studies.author: Josephs
studies.title: Large-scale dissociations between views of objects, scenes, and reachable-scale environments in visual cortex
studies.claim: PPA responds more strongly to scenes than to reachable-scale environments, and more strongly to reachable-scale environments than to objects.

studies.author: Zhao
studies.title: Turning an object into a scene: Buildings activate scene-selective visual cortex independently of visual features
studies.claim: PPA responds more strongly to buildings than to visually matched boxes.

studies.author: Epstein
studies.title: A cortical representation of the local visual environment
studies.claim: PPA responds as strongly to empty rooms as to the same rooms furnished, and more strongly to empty rooms than to arrays of objects with no spatial layout.

studies.author: Bar
studies.title: Cortical analysis of visual context
studies.claim: PPA responds more strongly to objects strongly associated with a specific context than to objects weakly associated with any context.

studies.author: Puce
studies.title: Face-sensitive regions in human extrastriate cortex studied by functional MRI
studies.claim: FFA responds more strongly to intact faces than to luminance-matched scrambled faces.

studies.author: Kanwisher
studies.title: The fusiform face area: A module in human extrastriate cortex specialized for face perception
studies.claim: FFA responds more strongly to faces than to objects or houses and more strongly to intact than scrambled faces.

studies.author: Kanwisher
studies.title: The effect of face inversion on the human fusiform face area
studies.claim: FFA responds more strongly to upright than inverted two-tone Mooney faces.

studies.author: Haxby
studies.title: The effect of face inversion on activity in human neural systems for face and object perception
studies.claim: Face inversion produces only a small change in the response of face-selective fusiform cortex.

studies.author: Tong
studies.title: Response properties of the human fusiform face area
studies.claim: FFA responds strongly across different face types, including human and cat faces, relative to objects.

studies.author: Wilkinson
studies.title: An fMRI study of the selective activation of human extrastriate form vision areas by radial and concentric gratings
studies.claim: FFA responds more strongly to concentric gratings than to radial or parallel gratings.

studies.author: Peelen
studies.title: Selectivity for the human body in the fusiform gyrus
studies.claim: Face-selective fusiform cortex responds strongly to headless human bodies as well as faces.

studies.author: Schwarzlose
studies.title: Separate face and body selectivity on the fusiform gyrus
studies.claim: FFA shows stronger selectivity for faces than for bodies, body parts, cars, or objects.

studies.author: Yue
studies.title: Lower-level stimulus features strongly influence responses in the fusiform face area
studies.claim: FFA responses to faces vary systematically with low-level properties including stimulus size and contrast.

studies.author: Brandman
studies.title: Bodies are represented as wholes rather than their sum of parts in the occipital-temporal cortex
studies.claim: FFA responds more strongly to a whole body with the head present than to the same parts scattered, and more strongly to a whole face than to scattered face parts.

studies.author: Kamps
studies.title: A face is more than just the eyes, nose, and mouth: fMRI evidence that face-selective cortex represents external features
studies.claim: FFA responds more strongly to arranged than rearranged face parts, for both internal and external features.

studies.author: Aguirre
studies.title: Stimulus inversion and the responses of face and object-sensitive cortical areas
studies.claim: FFA responds equally to upright and inverted faces, while responding more strongly to upright faces than to upright cars.

studies.author: Loffler
studies.title: fMRI evidence for the neural representation of faces
studies.claim: FFA responds more strongly to synthetic faces far from the mean face than to synthetic faces close to it.

studies.author: Brandman
studies.title: The body inversion effect is mediated by face-selective, not body-selective, mechanisms
studies.claim: FFA responds more strongly to upright than inverted faceless bodies when the head is present, but not when the head is removed.

studies.author: Liu
studies.title: Perception of face parts and face configurations: An fMRI study
studies.claim: FFA responds more strongly to real face parts than to black ovals in their place, and more strongly to the normal face layout than to a scrambled one.

studies.author: Brandman
studies.title: Bodies are represented as wholes rather than their sum of parts in the occipital-temporal cortex
studies.claim: EBA responds more strongly to a whole body than to the same body parts scattered; this whole-over-parts preference is absent for faces.

studies.author: Kamps
studies.title: A face is more than just the eyes, nose, and mouth: fMRI evidence that face-selective cortex represents external features
studies.claim: EBA responds more strongly to rearranged than arranged face-part crops.

studies.author: Taylor
studies.title: Functional MRI analysis of body and body part representations in the extrastriate and fusiform body areas
studies.claim: EBA responses become increasingly body-selective as progressively more of the body is shown.

studies.author: Lamm
studies.title: Is the extrastriate body area (EBA) sensitive to the perception of pain in others?
studies.claim: EBA responds similarly to images of hands undergoing painful and matched non-painful events.

studies.author: Cross
studies.title: Contorted and ordinary body postures in the human brain
studies.claim: EBA responds more strongly to contorted body postures than to ordinary body postures.

studies.author: Abassi
studies.title: The Representation of Two-Body Shapes in the Human Visual Cortex
studies.claim: EBA responds more strongly to two bodies facing each other than to the same bodies facing away.

studies.author: Gandolfo
studies.title: Converging evidence that left extrastriate body area supports visual sensitivity to social interactions
studies.claim: EBA responds more strongly to facing than non-facing human body dyads.

studies.author: Downing
studies.title: A cortical area selective for visual processing of the human body
studies.claim: EBA responds more strongly to human body parts than to object parts, but no more strongly to whole faces than to whole objects.

studies.author: Downing
studies.title: Domain specificity in visual cortex
studies.claim: EBA responds more strongly to headless human bodies than to any of 19 other categories, including mammals, the next most effective one.

studies.author: Morris
studies.title: Occipitotemporal activation evoked by the perception of human bodies is modulated by the presence or absence of the face
studies.claim: EBA responds more strongly to a body with the face hidden than to the same body with the face visible, and least to a face shown without the body.

studies.author: Sinke
studies.title: The constructive nature of affective vision: seeing fearful scenes activates extrastriate body area
studies.claim: EBA responds more strongly to fearful than to neutral scenes, even when no body or face is shown.

studies.author: Van den Stock
studies.title: Affective scenes influence fear perception of individual body expressions
studies.claim: EBA responds more strongly to a neutral body on a threatening scene than on a neutral scene, but shows no such scene effect for a fearful body.
